acceptance: The pre-cleanup inventory records the exact three remote branches and their clean linked worktrees: codex/canonical-lifecycle-parallel-alignment at .worktrees/canonical-lifecycle-parallel-alignment-20260817, codex/documentation-reader-receipt-lifecycle-cleanup-20260816 at .worktrees/pre-release-deprecated-assets-cleanup-current-main-20260816, and codex/verification-evidence-reuse-runtime-integration-20260817 at .worktrees/verification-evidence-reuse-runtime-integration-20260817.
The local-only backup/wi08-pre-base-reconcile branch is independently verified to have no worktree, no remote ref, no open PR, and preserved archive evidence before deletion.
Immediately before removal, all four exact target branch identities and the three linked worktrees are still clean, inactive, and unchanged; any mismatch fails closed.

The three exact linked worktrees are removed with Git worktree lifecycle commands, then their exact local branches and remote branches are deleted; no other branch, tag, release, or worktree is removed.
The user's detached parent worktree changes in Makefile and templates/make/Makefile.ai remain byte-for-byte untouched.

The target branch identities remain auditable through their recorded head commits and closed PR/provider records; current main retains the replacement archive for each target (PR #879 -> stale-work-item-delivery-reconciliation, PR #883 -> canonical-lifecycle-parallel-successor, verification runtime -> verification-evidence-reuse and later merged runtime commits), and the canonical predecessor's yellow needs_human_confirmation state is not reclassified as completed.

Post-cleanup checks return empty for the three target remote refs and four target local refs, `git worktree list --porcelain` contains none of the three target paths, the synchronized main worktree reports `main...origin/main` with no changes, `gh pr list --state open` returns no cleanup PR, and `gh issue list --state open` remains 0; the cleanup Work Item then completes its own archive/PR/merge/ai-close-work-item lifecycle.
guidelines: Do not modify Provider configuration or branch-protection settings.
Do not remove a worktree with uncommitted changes or an active Work Item Contract.
Use Git worktree commands so Git metadata and filesystem state are removed together.
Delete a non-merged branch only when its closed PR or archived Work Item is documented as obsolete and the exact replacement/retention evidence is preserved.

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Re-audit each exact path and ref immediately before removal, remove via Git commands, then compare before/after inventories.

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Verify no worktree/remote/PR ownership, preserve archive paths, delete only the exact local ref, and audit all remaining local refs.

intent.problem: The repository still retains branch identities and linked worktrees for historical Work Items after their delivery paths ended, so branch/worktree state no longer reflects the active governed work.
constraints: Delete only the exact clean and inactive identities inventoried before removal.
Preserve every archived Work Item evidence bundle, including incomplete or yellow historical Outcomes.
Protect the user's dirty parent worktree and do not alter provider configuration, tags, releases, or branch protection.
Use Git lifecycle commands and complete this cleanup as a normal Work Item through archive, PR, merge, and ai-close-work-item.
intent.rationale: A bounded, evidence-first cleanup restores the invariant that obsolete branch/worktree identities are removed without confusing cleanup with successful delivery or discarding recoverable Work Item evidence.
